title: Private Console: Network Access Policies + Cluster Upgrade Wizard
creator: Sofia Martinez
description: Design and validate a cohesive flow in the Redwood Console for operators managing Private/VPC clusters: (1) creating and editing Network Access Policies (CIDRs, peering, security groups, allow/deny rules), (2) assessing cluster health and scheduling rolling upgrades with canary/maintenance window controls, and (3) surfacing upgrade impact and cost delta. The intent is to reduce operator confusion during upgrades, minimize downtime risk, and make network configuration discoverable and auditable within the Private Console.
activity_log:
2026-02-10: Ticket created by Sofia Martinez — initial problem statement and goals.
2026-02-14: Kickoff with PM (Maya) and Eng (Ethan) — aligned on scope: Network Access Policy editor + Upgrade Wizard modal + Status page consolidation.
2026-02-18: Low-fidelity sketches reviewed (internal whiteboard). Trade-offs discussed: inline editing vs. dedicated modal, and exposing advanced CIDR matchers. Decision: primary UX will expose an \"Advanced\" toggle for operators who need fine-grained controls.
2026-02-25: Figma mid-fidelity prototype (v1) shared — focused on three paths: Add Policy, Edit Cluster Network, Schedule Upgrade. Link to prototype in assets.
2026-03-02: Design critique with Security (Priya) — feedback: require explicit audit log toggle in network changes, show KMS key used for cluster disk encryption on upgrade page, include pre-upgrade security checklist.
2026-03-05: Engineering review with runtime team — identified constraint: upgrade orchestration uses a rolling node drain API that cannot guarantee exact canary percentages; UI should avoid implying exactness.
2026-03-08: Second prototype (v2) adds explicit \"Estimated impact\" banner (text + confidence) and replaces percentage canary control with \"Canary nodes: small/medium/large\" presets.
2026-03-10: Usability test (5 participants: infra engineers at pilot customers) — results: users liked the one-click \"Dry Run\" to preview affected pods, asked for a visible upgrade timeline and per-node progress.
2026-03-12: Preparing this ticket for design handoff. Pending: finalize copy, create accessible components, and produce React-ready tokens and CSS spec.
decisions: 1) Use simplified, opinionated network policy editor by default; advanced CIDR/regex rules behind an 'Advanced' toggle. 2) Replace precise percentage canary control with discrete presets (small/medium/large) to align with runtime determinism. 3) Expose an immutable audit summary for any network change and surface KMS key reference on upgrade flows. 4) Provide a Dry Run preview and per-node upgrade progress on the status page.
next_steps: Finalize copy and microcopy for banners and confirmations
Export design tokens and component spec for engineering
Add acceptance criteria to GitHub PR (#4821)
Create lightweight accessibility test plan and run with AxE
notes: Accessibility: color contrast and keyboard-first flows for the editor. Localization: keep strings under 120 characters where possible. Performance: network rule validation should debounce API calls and perform client-side validation for obvious mistakes.
acceptance_criteria:
- Network Access Policy editor allows creating/editing/deleting rules with preview of affected clusters.
- Upgrade Wizard presents estimated impact, allows canary preset selection, scheduling (immediate/time-window), and Dry Run preview.
- Changes to network policies and upgrades produce audit entries and are visible in the status page within 1 minute.
- Engineering has component tokens and a working prototype (storybook) for handoff.
implementation_notes: Engineering: upgrade API will accept canary_preset values {small,medium,large} and return estimated node impact. Backend must emit audit event with change metadata and user. UI will poll status endpoint for per-node progress (500ms interval capped). Avoid exposing internal IPs; show masked CIDR labels for non-owner viewers.
archived_feedback: From pilot customer (FinTechOrg): wanted an option to automatically pause tenant traffic during node upgrades — added as backlog item PM-2207. From internal SRE: prefer maintenance window timezone selection in client locale — implemented in v2.
estimated_risks: Medium risk: incorrect upgrade messaging could lead to operator misconfiguration causing unexpected restarts. Mitigations: conservative defaults, explicit confirmations, and Dry Run mode.
final_status_notes: Ready for engineering handoff pending sign-off from Security (Priya) and Runtime lead (Ethan). Will split into two implementation PRs: network-editor (small) and upgrade-wizard (medium).
